title: Add JSONSchema strict response_format + improved validation errors (OpenAI compat)
author: Lina Chen
description:
Adds a first-class 'response_format' capability that supports JSON Schema validation with a strict_mode flag and OpenAI-compatible metadata. Motivation: customers want deterministic structured outputs and clearer, machine-actionable validation errors when LLM outputs don't match the expected schema. This PR implements the validation pipeline, improves error messages (codified error codes and locations), extends the OpenAI compatibility layer to accept 'response_format' parameters, and adds SDK surface updates and docs.

Key behaviors: strict_mode=true will cause the API to return a well-typed validation error (error.code: 'response_format.mismatch', plus path/location and a short hint) instead of best-effort correction. strict_mode=false will attempt best-effort repair by invoking the structured-output postprocessing flow (retry+formatting heuristics) and will surface the sanitization/actions performed in the response metadata. The implementation is consistent with the existing OpenAI compatibility layer: users can pass response_format in both Redwood native API and openai-compatible endpoints.

Rollout plan: feature-flag rollout (ff:jsonschema_strict_response) for 2 weeks, enable for internal traffic and opt-in customers, then open to public. Backwards compatibility: default behavior remains unchanged (best-effort repair). Breaking changes: none by default; strict_mode must be explicitly set to true to enforce strict validation.

Includes: 1) core validator implementation with streaming-aware validation hooks, 2) improved error model with codes and suggestion hints, 3) OpenAI-compatible request/response mapping and compatibility tests, 4) SDK clients (python/ts) additions and doc updates, 5) end-to-end tests and fuzzing harness updates.

Related: ENG-4820 (product spec), SUP-2175 (support cases that motivated improved error messages).

review_comments: Daniel Kim: Overall looks good. Can you clarify how the streaming validator behaves for very large responses? Specifically how partial failures are surfaced to the client?

Lina Chen: Streaming validator exposes partial_status events on the stream (metadata events). If strict_mode=true we abort at first definitive validation failure and emit a final 'response_format.mismatch' error payload. If strict_mode=false we continue and emit 'response_format.sanitized' metadata describing fixes.
Asha Patel: Please add a privacy check: when including sanitization hints we must not echo user data in error hints. Ensure hints are redacted for PII.
Lina Chen: Added redaction for hint strings and unit tests to validate redaction behavior.
Miguel Torres: Suggest adding an integration test that exercises the OpenAI compat layer so we don't regress the mapping behavior.
Lina Chen: Added compat integration job and documented the mapping in compat_mapper.go comments.
release_notes: Added 'response_format' JSON Schema support with a strict_mode option. strict_mode=true returns structured validation errors (error.code: response_format.mismatch). Added OpenAI compatibility for response_format. Default behavior unchanged (best-effort repair).
